"title": "Are There Mach Cones in Heavy Ion Collisions? Three-Particle Correlations from STAR",
"authors": "Jason Glyndwr Ulery for the STAR Collaboration",
"field_subfield": "High-energy nuclear physics (quark-gluon plasma / jet correlations)",
"type_of_paper": "Poster proceedings (experimental results)",
"executive_summary": "This poster presents STAR Collaboration measurements of three-particle azimuthal correlations in proton–proton (pp), deuterium–gold (d+Au), and gold–gold (Au+Au) collisions at a nucleon–nucleon center-of-mass energy of √sNN = 200 GeV. The analysis uses a hard trigger particle with transverse momentum 3 < pT < 4 GeV/c and two softer associated particles with 1 < pT < 2 GeV/c, all reconstructed in the STAR time projection chamber. The central scientific question is whether the observed off-diagonal structure in central Au+Au collisions reflects conical emission from Mach-cone shock waves generated by jet quenching, as opposed to alternative mechanisms such as simple QCD Cherenkov radiation or deflected jets. To isolate the genuine three-particle signal, the authors rigorously subtract combinatorial backgrounds: a hard-soft background built from the two-particle jet-like correlation folded with the normalized two-particle background, plus soft-soft and trigger-flow backgrounds constructed from mixed events. Systematic uncertainties from the flow-harmonic subtraction (v2 and v4) and from the background normalization are investigated in detail. The key finding is that off-diagonal peaks appear at approximately π ± 1.45 radians and grow with centrality, consistent with conical emission. Crucially, the emission angle shows no strong dependence on associated-particle pT, which favors Mach-cone emission over Cherenkov radiation, whose model predicts a sharply decreasing angle with increasing momentum. The signal is robust against variations in the v2 determination (reaction plane vs. four-particle cumulant) and against changes in the background normalization window. This work provides early quantitative evidence for collective conical flow in the quark-gluon plasma and establishes a methodology for disentangling conical emission from competing jet-quenching mechanisms.",

summary.title: Are There Mach Cones in Heavy Ion Collisions? Three-Particle Correlations from STAR
summary.authors: Jason Glyndwr Ulery for the STAR Collaboration
summary.field_subfield: High-energy nuclear physics (quark-gluon plasma / jet correlations)
summary.executive_summary: This poster presents STAR Collaboration measurements of three-particle azimuthal correlations in proton–proton (pp), deuterium–gold (d+Au), and gold–gold (Au+Au) collisions at a nucleon–nucleon center-of-mass energy of √sNN = 200 GeV. The analysis uses a hard trigger particle with transverse momentum 3 < pT < 4 GeV/c and two softer associated particles with 1 < pT < 2 GeV/c, all reconstructed in the STAR time projection chamber. The central scientific question is whether the observed off-diagonal structure in central Au+Au collisions reflects conical emission from Mach-cone shock waves generated by jet quenching, as opposed to alternative mechanisms such as simple QCD Cherenkov radiation or deflected jets. To isolate the genuine three-particle signal, the authors rigorously subtract combinatorial backgrounds: a hard-soft background built from the two-particle jet-like correlation folded with the normalized two-particle background, plus soft-soft and trigger-flow backgrounds constructed from mixed events. Systematic uncertainties from the flow-harmonic subtraction (v2 and v4) and from the background normalization are investigated in detail. The key finding is that off-diagonal peaks appear at approximately π ± 1.45 radians and grow with centrality, consistent with conical emission. Crucially, the emission angle shows no strong dependence on associated-particle pT, which favors Mach-cone emission over Cherenkov radiation, whose model predicts a sharply decreasing angle with increasing momentum. The signal is robust against variations in the v2 determination (reaction plane vs. four-particle cumulant) and against changes in the background normalization window. This work provides early quantitative evidence for collective conical flow in the quark-gluon plasma and establishes a methodology for disentangling conical emission from competing jet-quenching mechanisms.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This poster presents STAR Collaboration measurements of three-particle azimuthal correlations in proton–proton (pp), deuterium–gold (d+Au), and gold–gold (Au+Au) collisions at a nucleon–nucleon center-of-mass energy of √sNN = 200 GeV. The analysis uses a hard trigger particle with transverse momentum 3 < pT < 4 GeV/c and two softer associated particles with 1 < pT < 2 GeV/c, all reconstructed in the STAR time projection chamber. The central scientific question is whether the observed off-diagonal structure in central Au+Au collisions reflects conical emission from Mach-cone shock waves generated by jet quenching, as opposed to alternative mechanisms such as simple QCD Cherenkov radiation or deflected jets. To isolate the genuine three-particle signal, the authors rigorously subtract combinatorial backgrounds: a hard-soft background built from the two-particle jet-like correlation folded with the normalized two-particle background, plus soft-soft and trigger-flow backgrounds constructed from mixed events. Systematic uncertainties from the flow-harmonic subtraction (v2 and v4) and from the background normalization are investigated in detail. The key finding is that off-diagonal peaks appear at approximately π ± 1.45 radians and grow with centrality, consistent with conical emission. Crucially, the emission angle shows no strong dependence on associated-particle pT, which favors Mach-cone emission over Cherenkov radiation, whose model predicts a sharply decreasing angle with increasing momentum. The signal is robust against variations in the v2 determination (reaction plane vs. four-particle cumulant) and against changes in the background normalization window. This work provides early quantitative evidence for collective conical flow in the quark-gluon plasma and establishes a methodology for disentangling conical emission from competing jet-quenching mechanisms.

Research Context
Heavy-ion collisions may create a quark-gluon plasma that can be studied through jets and jet correlations. Two-particle azimuthal correlations reveal an away-side structure that is broadened or double-humped in central collisions. The broad away-side structure is consistent with many competing physics mechanisms. Hydrodynamic conical flow from Mach-cone shock waves is one such candidate mechanism. Cherenkov radiation is another candidate that also produces conical emission. Three-particle correlations can differentiate conical emission from other mechanisms. The associated-particle pT dependence of the conical angle distinguishes hydrodynamic conical flow from simple Cherenkov radiation.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is whether conical emission from Mach-cone shock waves is present in heavy-ion collisions. Three-particle correlations are hypothesized to reveal conical emission as off-diagonal structure at π ± ~1.45 radians. The off-diagonal signal is expected to increase in magnitude with collision centrality. Conical flow is hypothesized to produce an emission angle independent of associated-particle pT. Cherenkov radiation is hypothesized to produce an emission angle sharply decreasing with increasing associated-particle momentum. Deflected jets are hypothesized to contribute to on-diagonal broadening but not to off-diagonal conical structure. The predicted outcome is a pT-independent angle favoring Mach-cone emission over Cherenkov radiation.

Methodological Details
The study reports results from the STAR experiment at RHIC. Measurements span pp, d+Au, and Au+Au collision systems. All collisions were at a nucleon-nucleon energy of √sNN = 200 GeV. The trigger particle has transverse momentum in the range 3 < pT < 4 GeV/c. The two associated particles have transverse momentum in the range 1 < pT < 2 GeV/c. All particles are charged and reconstructed in the STAR time projection chamber. The analysis treats events as a sum of jet-like correlated and background components. The hard-soft background is built from the two-particle jet-like correlation folded with the normalized two-particle background. The two-particle background is constructed by mixing events with flow modulation added pairwise from average v2 values. The v4 contribution uses the parameterization v4 = 1.15 v2². The background is normalized within 0.8 < |Δφ| < 1.2 using the zero-yield-at-one-radian method. The soft-soft background is obtained from mixed events in the same centrality window. The trigger-flow background is added triplet-wise from mixed events. The total background is ˆJ2 ⊗αBinc2 + βα²(Binc3 + Binc,TF3). The scale factor β is obtained so that associated pairs in the three-particle signal equal the square of associated particles in the two-particle signal. Centrality classes include 50-80%, 30-50%, 10-30%, 0-10%, and ZDC-triggered 0-12% Au+Au. High-statistics central data uses an online ZDC trigger. The off-diagonal peak location is determined from a double Gaussian fit to an off-diagonal strip projection.

Procedures And Architectures
The raw three-particle distribution is plotted in ΔφaT = φa − φT and ΔφbT = φb − φT. The off-diagonal peak location is found to be 1.45 radians from π. Average signals are computed in 0.7 × 0.7 boxes at specific angular regions. On-diagonal and off-diagonal regions are compared to isolate conical emission from deflected jets. The off-diagonal peak angle is measured as a function of associated-particle pT. The off-diagonal peak angle is measured as a function of centrality. The off-diagonal peak angle is determined from double Gaussian fits. Statistical errors are shown as solid bars and systematic errors as shaded regions. The reaction-plane v2 and four-particle cumulant v2 are used as upper and lower bounds for the systematic uncertainty. The normalization window is varied by doubling it to 0.6 < |Δφ| < 1.4. A 20% effect on trigger-particle v2 arises from requiring a correlated particle. The π/2 reference line is shown on the emission-angle plots.

Key Results
Background-subtracted three-particle signals show near-side, away-side, and mixed-side peaks in pp and d+Au. The away-side peak displays diagonal elongation consistent with kT broadening in pp and d+Au. Peripheral Au+Au shows additional on-diagonal elongation possibly due to deflected jets. Central Au+Au collisions display an off-diagonal structure at about π ± 1.45 radians. The off-diagonal signal increases in magnitude with centrality. The off-diagonal signals significantly deviate from zero in central Au+Au collisions. The ZDC-triggered 0-12% central data shows the most prominent off-diagonal structure. The difference between on-diagonal and off-diagonal signals decreases with distance from (π,π). The off-diagonal peak angle is consistent with a constant as a function of associated-particle pT. The Au+Au 0-12% cone angle is measured at 1.41 ± 0.02 radians. The Au+Au 0-50% cone angle is measured at 1.45 ± 0.03 radians. The off-diagonal peak angle is consistent with remaining constant as a function of centrality. The constant-fit cone angle is 1.46 ± 0.03 radians. The signal is robust with respect to the v2 determination method. The variations in hard-soft and trigger-flow backgrounds cancel to first order in the sum. The signal is robust with respect to the change in normalization window. No strong pT dependence of the angles on associated-particle pT is observed. The overall result is consistent with Mach cone emission.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The off-diagonal peaks at π ± 1.45 radians are interpreted as evidence for conical emission. The pT-independent emission angle supports hydrodynamic conical flow from Mach-cone shock waves. The constant angle disfavors simple Cherenkov radiation, which predicts a sharply decreasing angle. The on-diagonal excess is attributed to deflected jets in addition to conical emission. The difference between on- and off-diagonal signals quantifies the deflected-jet contribution. The robustness of the signal supports the reliability of the background subtraction. The findings suggest the quark-gluon plasma supports collective conical flow. The method provides a framework for disentangling conical emission from competing jet-quenching mechanisms.

Contradictions And Limitations
The conical-emission interpretation is not definitive and remains consistent with alternative mechanisms. The off-diagonal structure may be contaminated by deflected jets, complicating the interpretation. The v4 parameterization is a simplifying assumption that introduces uncertainty. The default v2 is an average of two methods, and the systematic uncertainty is estimated from their spread. The 20% trigger-particle v2 effect from requiring a correlated particle is a source of systematic uncertainty. The v4 parameterization v4 = 1.15 v2² is adopted from the data and may not capture all correlations. The multiplicity bias from requiring a trigger particle is corrected by α2 but may not be fully accounted for. The exact number of events or luminosity is not reported, limiting reproducibility. The analysis relies on the STAR TPC detector, which may limit particle identification. The poster format limits the level of detail available for full replication.

Claims
Off-diagonal three-particle correlations at π ± 1.45 radians indicate conical emission in central Au+Au collisions. Off-diagonal structure appears at about π ± 1.45 radians. The off-diagonal signal increases with centrality. The off-diagonal signals significantly deviate from zero in central collisions. The off-diagonal peak angle is consistent with a constant. The off-diagonal structure may be contaminated by deflected jets. The off-diagonal and on-diagonal signals both receive contributions from conical emission and deflected jets. The result supports the existence of collective conical flow in the quark-gluon plasma. The method enables differentiation of conical emission from other mechanisms.
The emission angle is independent of associated-particle pT, favoring Mach-cone emission over Cherenkov radiation. The angle is consistent with constant as a function of associated particle pT. The constant-fit cone angle is 1.46 ± 0.03 radians. The angle is consistent with remaining constant as a function of centrality. No strong pT dependence of the angles on associated-particle pT is observed. Cherenkov radiation predicts a sharply decreasing angle with increasing momentum. The pT-independent angle is consistent with Mach cone emission. The associated-particle pT dependence distinguishes hydrodynamic conical flow from simple Cherenkov radiation.
The background subtraction and signal are robust against systematic variations. The signal is robust with respect to the v2 determination method. The variations in backgrounds cancel to first order in the sum. The signal is robust with respect to the change in normalization window. The hard-soft and trigger-flow backgrounds individually vary a great deal with the change in elliptic flow. The systematic uncertainties are dominated by the flow measurement and normalization.

Data And Code Availability
The data were taken in the STAR time projection chamber at RHIC. The data are from pp, d+Au, and Au+Au collisions at √sNN = 200 GeV.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The signal is robust with respect to the v2 determination method. The reaction-plane and four-particle cumulant v2 are used as upper and lower bounds. The variations in backgrounds cancel to first order in the sum. The signal is robust with respect to the change in normalization window. The normalization window was doubled to 0.6 < |Δφ| < 1.4. The 20% trigger-particle v2 effect from requiring a correlated particle is a systematic.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows raw two- and three-particle azimuthal distributions and backgrounds. Figure 2 shows background-subtracted three-particle correlations across centrality classes. Figure 3 shows average signals in 0.7 × 0.7 boxes and differences between on- and off-diagonal regions. Figure 4 shows away-side strip projections for d+Au and ZDC-triggered Au+Au. Figure 5 shows emission angles as functions of associated-particle pT and centrality. Figure 6 shows systematic checks for reaction-plane v2, four-particle cumulant v2, and normalization. Figure 1a shows the raw two-particle correlation and mixed-event background.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the observation of off-diagonal three-particle correlations at π ± 1.45 radians consistent with conical emission. 2. The strongest evidence is the pT-independent emission angle of 1.46 ± 0.03 radians favoring Mach-cone emission. 3. The future path is to refine the background subtraction and disentangle conical emission from deflected jets.
